title: Pound and Rebka, "Apparent Weight of Photons" (1960)
summary: R. V. Pound and G. A. Rebka reported in Physical Review Letters in April 1960 a measurement of the effect of gravitational potential on the apparent frequency of electromagnetic radiation, using recoil-free 14.4 keV gamma rays from Co-57 absorbed in Fe-57.
body: In Physical Review Letters volume 4, pages 337–341, dated 1 April 1960, R. V. Pound and G. A. Rebka of Harvard University published "Apparent Weight of Photons". The abstract reproduced in the U.S. Department of Energy OSTI record states: "The effect of gravitational potential on the apparent frequency of electro-magnetic radiation was measured by using the sharply defined energy of recoil-free 14.4kev gamma rays emitted by Co/sup 57/ and absorbed in Fe/sup 57/." That abstract also gives a measured mean gravitational shift in frequency together with a stated uncertainty of 0.6. The DOI registration record supplies the title, both authors, the journal name, the volume and the page range 337–341. The paper is five pages long.
